name: Sclerotinia Timber Rot
symptoms: White cotton-like fungal growth on stems Stem rot or dry decay (timber-like appearance) Black seed-like sclerotia inside or on stems Yellowing and wilting of leaves Plants collapsing due to stem damage
description: Sclerotinia timber rot is a fungal disease that causes severe stem decay in many crops. The fungus produces white cotton-like mold and black survival bodies called sclerotia. Infected stems become dry or rotten, leading to plant wilting and collapse.
management: Rotate crops with non-host plants Improve spacing and airflow between plants Remove and destroy infected plant debris Avoid excessive irrigation
prevention: Use clean seeds and healthy transplants Monitor crops during cool and wet weather Apply integrated disease management practices
